title: Acceptance Sandbox + Compatibility Signer for External Community Checkpoints
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Build an isolated acceptance sandbox and a deterministic compatibility signer that produces a machine-verifiable artifact for community-provided checkpoints. This ticket codifies the end-to-end flow: ingest external weights -> run deterministic conversion + lightweight smoke workloads in a sandboxed runner -> produce a signed compatibility manifest (signer artifact) with runtime hints and quality signals -> publish artifact to the intake catalog for downstream profiling and pinning stages.

Why: Current onboarding admits many artifacts into the pipeline that later fail in profiling due to subtle conversion or operator mismatches. Creating an early, reproducible compatibility signal reduces wasted CI, surfaces quick rejections, and provides a clear signed contract for runtime mapping and fallback behavior.

Acceptance criteria:
- A sandboxed runner (K8s job) that can perform a standard conversion + smoke set within 30 minutes on a standard staging GPU node (p4d-like).
- Deterministic output: the compatibility signer must produce the same manifest (byte-for-byte) for a given artifact and conversion parameters.
- Manifest includes: canonical checksum, minimal working sequence length, tokenization fingerprint, quantization-safety flag, recommended kernel family, suggested KV cache memory budget, and three simple quality signals (perplexity on a short testset, top-k token overlap to reference, and a generation smoke-check pass/fail).
- Signed manifest format (ed25519) integrated with existing Artifact Gateway keyring (Galley).
- Telemetry emitted for acceptance latency, pass/fail rate, and top-3 failure classes to Console (per-route onboarding dashboard).
- Integration tests and one end-to-end demo workflow that takes a community checkpoint from S3 -> signed manifest in the intake catalog.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Determinism vs coverage: We intentionally limit the sandbox smoke set to small canonical prompts to keep runtime bounded and deterministic across hardware. This reduces early coverage but improves repeatability and speed.
- Signing model: Using ed25519 via Galley KMS key simplifies verification; it does require a small ops process to rotate keys and extend access to on-prem image runners.
- Manifest scope: Keep manifest minimal so later profiling is not duplicated; runtime hints (kernel families, kv budgets) are advisory only and can be overridden by Dedicated policies.

High-level flow:
1) Artifact Gateway stores incoming checkpoint and triggers Intake Worker.
2) Intake Worker launches a sandbox conversion job with pinned converter container and deterministic RNG seeds.
3) Conversion outputs a normalized model package and small smoke-run traces.
4) Sandbox runner executes smoke workloads and computes quality signals.
5) Signer composes the manifest and signs with Galley key and publishes to intake catalog.
6) Downstream onboarding (profiling and pin recommendation) consumes the manifest and may fast-fail incompatible artifacts.

Runbooks / links:
- Confluence design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INFER/pages/78541234/Acceptance+Sandbox+Design+Doc
- Intake catalog schema (proto): https://github.com/redwood-inference/artifact-schema/blob/main/proto/intake_manifest.proto
- PoC sandbox runner PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-runner/pull/197
- Galley signer integration PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/galley/pull/432
- Demo notebook (S3 -> signed manifest): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Xb-demo-notebook/view

QA plan:
- Unit tests for signer determinism (run 5x across different runner images).
- Integration smoke test: checkpoint from huggingface-sample -> signed manifest within CI (timeout 45m).
- Fault injection: simulate corrupted weights and ensure sandbox fails fast and reports failure class.

Rollout plan:
- Phase A (staging): run on a subset of community checkpoints (weekly ingestion cadence) and surface metrics in onboarding dashboard.
- Phase B (limited prod): gating new community artifacts by signed manifest; artifacts without manifest remain in a lower-priority queue for manual triage.
- Phase C (enforced): the manifest becomes required for automated profiling and pinning.

Risks and mitigations:
- False negatives (good models rejected): mitigate by allowing manual overrides and an audit trail in the console; preserve raw artifacts for deep analysis.
- Key management for signing across on-prem runners: engage Security to document HSM/KMS policy and ephemeral signing proxies.
- Runtime differences across GPUs: include kernel-family suggestion only as advisory and pass a compatibility score instead of hard deny.

Next steps (technical):
- Finalize manifest proto with PM and Runtime engineers (owner: R. Patel).
- Complete Galley signer PR and key access runbook (owner: S. Chen, Security).
- Add telemetry hooks to Console onboarding dashboard (owner: M. Alvarez).

Related tickets: ENG-41807 (artifact-gateway with compatibility matrix) and ENG-36120 (automated-variant-validation harness).
